text:
Hurricanes continue preseason camp with focus on growth and team chemistry
The Miami Hurricanes continued their preseason preparations Tuesday on the Greentree Practice Fields in Coral Gables as the third week of camp progressed, according to an Aug. 18 report. Several players spoke with reporters after practice to discuss the team's development ahead of its Sept. 4 opener at Stanford.
Offensive lineman Matt McCoy commented on the progress of freshmen Jackson Cantwell and Ben Congdon, saying, “Ben and Jackson are doing a phenomenal job and they’re coming up to me [with questions]. It’s not even like I’m getting them going – they’re asking me. They’re always coming up to me, making sure they’re doing this right and that right, whatever it is. And they’re doing a phenomenal job. They’re growing men about their business. They’re not freshmen at all.” McCoy also praised fellow lineman Ryan Rodriguez for his leadership: “He’s making sure everybody’s on point. He’s being that guy for us, a leader upfront.”
Defensive back Zechariah Poyser discussed the impact of younger teammates JJ Dunnigan and Bryce Fitzgerald: “I think they’re both different players, but both [are] very good players, for sure... I think he’ll have a big role this year and I’m excited to see what he’s going to do.” Poyser said communication has improved in Corey Hetherman’s defensive system: “It’s like secondhand nature because... this is my second year in the defense. The communication has gotten way better from day one.”
Linebacker Chase Smith reflected on how scrimmages aid preparation: “[They] give us a really good judgment on exactly what we have to fix as far as on the field and really in between these meetings.” Smith noted growth among sophomore linebackers Ezekiel Marcelin Jr. and Kellen Wiley Jr., stating their mental approach has progressed significantly.
Ryan Rodriguez emphasized cross-training along the offensive line: “One of the best ways to learn all the positions on the offensive line is just play them all... It just builds chemistry together.” He also said there is still work ahead following last week’s scrimmage but stressed maintaining high standards set by previous teams.
The Hurricanes will continue camp as they prepare for their season opener against Stanford.
